description: Secondary eval (B): generalization probe on UNSEEN tasks. Two pools (in_dist, heldout-camera), 8 tasks x 3 episodes = 24 episodes per arm per pool, seed=42 so the task pool AND initial conditions are identical across arms (a paired design). Source: Drive eval_out_t4/<arm>/<mode>/result.json (sft/rs_sft/dpo run 2026-07-24; grpo run 2026-07-25 on a rebuilt Colab VM with the same command/seed). NOTE: per-EPISODE outcomes were not retained by eval_heldout (episodes:[] in result.json), so the paired analysis here is at TASK level (per-task success counts out of 3), not episode level.

paired_vs_sft_task_level.comment: Task-clustered bootstrap (seed=12345, 20000 resamples) of the mean per-task success-rate difference vs SFT, plus an exact sign test on tasks where the arm beats / loses to SFT. EVERY interval includes zero: no arm is significantly better than SFT on either unseen pool. The GRPO point estimates are the highest but the ordering is NOT statistically established.

robustness_note: GRPO's in_dist 29.2% is concentrated: 6 of its 7 successes come from two tasks at 3/3 (51, 1894). Excluding those two tasks entirely leaves 1 success in the remaining 6 tasks (1/18 = 5.6%), below SFT's 1/18 on the same six. The heldout 20.8% is spread across five distinct tasks (935, 665, 620, 748, 679 at 1/3 each) and is correspondingly more stable (tighter CI). The two GRPO numbers therefore have opposite robustness profiles and should not be presented as an equivalent pair.
caveats: The in_dist and heldout pools are DIFFERENT unseen task sets, so their difference conflates viewpoint sensitivity with task difficulty; only within-pool cross-arm comparisons are meaningful.
The secondary winner (GRPO) is selected post hoc as the max over 4 arms in each of 2 pools, with no multiplicity control -- hypothesis-generating only.
Per-episode outcomes were not retained, so an episode-level McNemar (as used for the primary eval) is not possible for this probe.
